title: Book 1, Aphorisms 1–37
author: Francis Bacon
source: *Novum Organum*, Book 1, Aphorisms 1–37, in the English translation edited by Joseph Devey (New York: P. F. Collier & Son, 1902), 11–19. Bacon published the *Novum Organum* in Latin in 1620.
summary: Man as nature's minister and interpreter: knowledge and power are one, but the sciences and the syllogism are useless for discovery, and notions hastily abstracted from things are confused. There are two ways of searching for truth, one flying from particulars to the most general axioms, the other rising by degrees, and Bacon contrasts the anticipations of the mind with the interpretation of nature.
